freeze_rules.source_evidence_basis: Previously verified local article evidence, converted to short original public-safe factual paraphrases with retained source references.

evidence.text: History Workshop discusses the Radar Key as a small key connected with disabled people's access to locked public toilets in the United Kingdom.
It was designed to provide disabled people with access to public toilets.
The article presents the key as an artefact of disabled people's activism since the late twentieth century.
AAPD's article identifies Lois Curtis and Elaine Wilson and says they lived in Georgia Regional Hospital.
They had psychiatric, intellectual and developmental disabilities.
The Olmstead decision found that unjustified institutionalisation violates the Americans with Disabilities Act.

articles.title: FRAME SHIFT 2026 Will Feature Works by Deaf and Disabled Artists
articles.prior_source_sha256: not separately recorded in retained packet

evidence.text: Accessible Arts and Sydney Opera House planned to present FRAME SHIFT films and video artworks by Deaf and Disabled artists in December 2026.
All artworks in the selection were to be captioned, Auslan interpreted and audio described.
The announced selection included three newly commissioned works.

articles.title: Will the House of Lords improve accessibility in the Railways Bill?

evidence.text: Transport for All says the Railways Bill was before the House of Lords, where peers were debating amendments affecting disabled passengers.
It argues that a duty to promote accessibility or consider disabled passengers' needs is weaker than a clear legal duty to improve accessibility.
Proposed changes included accessibility duties and engagement with accessibility stakeholders.
NV Access announced that NVDA 2026.3, its free screen reader for Microsoft Windows, was available to download.
The update added new braille tables for several languages and variants.
Its updated browsable-message dialog better supports resizing, maximising and minimising.

articles.title: Meta AI Glasses Help Make Art More Accessible for People Who Are Blind or With Low Vision.

evidence.text: An Italian museum used AI-powered smart glasses to provide audio descriptions for visitors who are blind or have low vision.
The glasses recognise an artwork and provide spoken descriptions through speakers in the frames.
The experience covered eight artworks and was developed with input from blind and low-vision people and Italian organisations.
